title: Spec 122 §1.10 archetype census — every remaining step, declared
description: WF1 'conversion roadmap' (2026-09-10). Ask A3's data half: an unconverted or pending file's archetype is DECLARED data, never inferred from its name. Rows cover every one of the 55 currently-unconverted files (scripts/steps/_schema/converted.json is NOT re-listed here — a converted step's own descriptor.identity.archetype is the authoritative source, provenance rule 1) plus the ONE pending file (enrich-parcels.js), which has a real descriptor but is not yet registered in converted.json's own `converted[]` array. archetype is one of the 8 canonical values (Spec 122 §1.10) or the literal string "UNDECLARED" — never silently absent (Ask A3: the 36 non-`sources` files have no archetype and no PH-2 risk data yet; ARCH-CENSUS is their own future WF, not this one).

exemptions.description: A manifest.scripts slug the conversion programme will never convert is DECLARED here, explicitly, rather than silently dropped from the totality this census/roadmap otherwise enforces. TWO grounds, not one. (a) Ask A2 (operator ruling, 2026-09-10) — no JS file to convert at all: a `.py` step (`python_step_excluded`), or a `coming_soon` entry with file:null (`no_file`). (b) Spec 124 §5 R-AP (2026-09-15) — `runner_owned`: the JS file EXISTS, but the concern it implements belongs to THE RUNNER (Spec 122 §4 / §7.3 concern row 4 / §7.4 A3), which declares nothing per step and cannot be opted out of, so there is no descriptor, no identity.archetype and no x-profile to write. `runner_owned` is the ONLY reason permitted to name a real JS file, and generate-conversion-roadmap.mjs enforces that both directions. Rendered in its own 'Declared exemptions' table by the generator and folded into a slug-grain totality identity — `<manifest slugs> = <converted> + <pending> + <exempted> + <remaining>`, every term DERIVED from its own registry (Spec 124 R-AN), never retyped — so the count is provably exhaustive rather than just the remainder.

file.description: manifest.scripts[slug].file verbatim — a string ending .py, or the literal null a coming_soon entry declares. The generator throws if this disagrees with the live manifest.

reason.description: python_step_excluded = operator ruling 2026-09-10: the Python step (aic-orchestrator.py) is EXCLUDED from the conversion programme entirely — not deferred to any future batch, out of the JS step standard's scope by design, stays on its own runner. no_file = a coming_soon manifest entry with file:null — nothing exists yet to convert. runner_owned = Spec 124 §5 R-AP (2026-09-15): the slug HAS a real JS file, but the concern it implements is owned by THE RUNNER (Spec 122 §4 / §7.3 concern row 4 / §7.4 A3) — "nothing is declared per step, and a step cannot opt out" — so there is no per-step descriptor, no identity.archetype in step.schema.json's 8-value enum, and no x-profile. It is the ONLY reason that may name a real JS file, and the generator throws both directions (a real JS file under any other reason; a runner_owned row with no real JS file).

ruling.description: The operator ruling that made this a permanent exemption, e.g. "operator 2026-09-10".

scope.description: What the exemption covers / does not cover, e.g. "out of the JS step standard; stays on its own runner".

slug.description: manifest.scripts registry key. A slug with no such key is a schema violation the generator refuses to emit over (never silently skipped).

file.description: Must equal manifest.scripts[slug].file exactly — the generator throws otherwise (converted ⊆ manifest files, this census's own analogue).

archetype.description: One of Spec 122 §1.10's 8 canonical archetypes, or the literal "UNDECLARED" — a real, explicit row stating the census does not (yet) know, never an absent row a reader could mistake for an oversight.

batch.description: The roadmap batch this file belongs to. "pending" is reserved for the ONE file registered in converted.json's pending[] (enrich-parcels.js) — tracked here, not double-counted against the 55 unconverted total.

reason.description: Why this archetype (or UNDECLARED) — a spec citation, a real descriptor path, or 'deferred to ARCH-CENSUS (Ask A3)'. Required for every row, real archetype or not — mirrors programme-items.json's evidence requirement: a NOT_STARTED/UNDECLARED row still needs the measurement that PROVES the absence, never empty.

status.description: RETENTION (Spec 124 §5 R-AO, added 2026-09-15). Absent = a remaining/pending row, the original shape. `"converted"` = the row was RETAINED through cutover instead of deleted. Before this, commit 9 DELETED a slug's census row, which made fast invariant #25 ARCHETYPE-PARITY unreachable for its own founding case: with no row left, `censusArchetype` is null for every converted slug and a valid-but-wrong archetype passes silently (proved by swapping `load_ravines` to ASSERT — still PASS). A retained row's `archetype` is the census's OWN pre-cutover value and MUST NOT be re-derived from the descriptor: the whole point is that #25 compares two independently-authored facts. The generator enforces both directions — a `"converted"` row whose file is not in converted.json throws, and a row with no `status` whose file IS converted throws.

converted_at.description: The commit-9 cutover SHA this row was converted at (short or full). Required whenever `status` is `"converted"`, forbidden otherwise — a retention claim carries the commit that makes it checkable.
